exposure: mode of delivery (Caesarean Section, vaginal birth)
cohort: The study included women with singleton neonates delivered between 22 and <37 weeks of gestation, with samples of 15,471 from the WHO Global Survey and 15,053 from the WHO Multi-country Survey.
finding: Caesarean section in preterm births was associated with both increased odds of maternal and neonatal intensive care unit admission and maternal near miss, but significantly decreased odds of fresh stillbirth and perinatal death compared to vaginal birth.
mod_finding: Compared to vaginal birth, Caesarean section in preterm births was associated with significantly increased odds of maternal intensive care unit admission, maternal near miss, and neonatal intensive care unit admission, but significantly decreased odds of fresh stillbirth and perinatal death.
